I saved the answers to `answer.json`. Answer a depends on an assumption you should confirm (see the note below).

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | `consumer`, 294,145,157 won |
| b. Customers with at least one paid Q3 order | 246 |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | `sw`, 271,374,888 won |
| d. Month with the highest net sales overall | `2025-09` (290,254,127 won) |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refunds | `u56@ex.com` (1,711,715 won; 2nd place is 1,707,900 won, so no tie) |
| f. Customers with two or more paid Q3 orders | 225 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 677,049 won (819,229,808 won ÷ 1,210 orders) |
| h. Growth from August to September | 11.9% (259,327,310 → 290,254,127; unrounded 11.9258%) |

**How I counted**
- I converted order times from UTC to KST before deciding dates and months. Q3 is KST 2025-07-01 00:00 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01.
- Only orders with status `paid` count. I rounded each line amount and each refund unit price down to the won.
- Segments are trimmed and lowercased, which leaves three: smb, enterprise and consumer.
- For b, e and f, accounts with the same email count as one person. There are 300 accounts but 250 unique emails.

**Data checks:** The data looked clean. There were no orphan keys, no refunds larger than the quantity ordered, no duplicate refunds and no out-of-range discounts.

**Note on answer a:** 26 emails have accounts in different segments. I credited each order to the segment of the account that placed it. If you give each person a single segment instead, the winner changes with the rule you pick:
- **Each account's own segment (what I used):** consumer, 294,145,157 won
- **Segment of the oldest account (smallest id):** enterprise, 286,846,126 won
- **Segment of the most recently joined account:** consumer, 296,738,398 won

Your definitions only say how to count customers, not how to assign a segment, so I used each account's own segment. If you want one segment per person, tell me which rule and I'll update answer a.
